newsitem.title: FRANCE: Car bomb kills one, wounds 10 in Algiers hotel.
newsitem.headline: Car bomb kills one, wounds 10 in Algiers hotel.

text.p: A car bomb exploded early on Tuesday in front of a hotel in central Algiers killing one people and wounding 10 others, Algerian security forces said.
The security forces did not elaborate in their statement read on Algerian state-run radio.
Eyewitnesses, speaking by telephone from Algiers, said the bomb went off at about 05.45 a.m. (04.45 GMT), by the Hotel Angleterre in downtown Algiers, badly damaging the hotel.
They said they saw several people at the scene who had been wounded.
An Algiers's resident said he has heard the blast from his house located in a suburb, four km (2.5 miles) away from the explosion scene.

An estimated 50,000 people have died in violence pitting Moslem rebels against government forces since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a commanding lead.
